dimensions.conditions: Peaceful expression; a formal political petition needs written, respectful submission.

dimensions.conditions: Ordinary advocacy is distinct from a constitutionally enforceable political petition; observe personal-data rules and Chamber lobbying rules if influencing legislative decisions.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts. 8, 9; Chamber of Deputies Rules arts. 263–264

dimensions.conditions: A foreign entity’s policy advocacy may count as prohibited political interference; the texts do not establish whether every factual/policy message by a foreign legal entity crosses that line. Do not treat this as permission to intervene.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts. 8, 33; Political Parties Law arts. 25(1)(i), 54(1)(d)

dimensions.conditions: Where communication amounts to interference in Mexico’s political affairs; nonpolitical inquiries are not categorically prohibited.

dimensions.conditions: General expression may be lawful; unsolicited collection/reuse of personally identifying handles or messaging lists must comply with privacy principles; social posts are not automatically formal petitions.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts. 6, 8; Private-Sector Personal Data Law arts. 5, 9, 15–16

dimensions.conditions: Automation does not create a separate blanket prohibition; controller of bulk address lists must satisfy applicable personal-data purpose, notice, public-source exception and opposition rules. Do not infer that public contact listings permit unrestricted bulk messages.
dimensions.legal_basis: Federal Law on Personal Data Protection Held by Private Parties arts. 5, 9(II), 15–16, 28–30

dimensions.conditions: For enforceable access to existing records, direct request to the office’s Transparency Unit; a personal email to an elected official is not necessarily such a request. No general duty to create a new fact-check.
dimensions.legal_basis: General Transparency Law arts. 123–126

dimensions.conditions: Any person may request existing public records via the Transparency Unit; distinguish a neutral fact request from intervention in political affairs. No general duty to adjudicate the claim.
dimensions.legal_basis: General Transparency Law arts. 123–126; Constitution art. 33

dimensions.conditions: Submit request for existing documented information to the Transparency Unit; postal mail is expressly recognized.
dimensions.legal_basis: General Transparency Law arts. 123–125

dimensions.conditions: Use National Transparency Platform for existing information; nationality or proof of interest not required.
dimensions.legal_basis: General Transparency Law arts. 14, 124–126

dimensions.conditions: Verbal request to Transparency Unit is recognized; unit records and assigns a folio. This does not require creation of a new factual analysis.
dimensions.legal_basis: General Transparency Law arts. 124–126

dimensions.conditions: No general statutory designation of a social-media bot message as a formal access request; use approved channels instead.
dimensions.legal_basis: General Transparency Law art. 124

dimensions.conditions: Written, peaceful and respectful political petition addressed to competent public authority; written response in a brief period.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution art. 8

dimensions.conditions: Written respectful petition; for federal administrative proceedings electronic submission is effective where agency enables it by published general rules with electronic identification.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution art. 8; Federal Administrative Procedure Law arts. 15, 69-C

dimensions.conditions: Use officially enabled/authenticated procedure; an arbitrary web form does not automatically fulfill formal administrative requirements.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution art. 8; Federal Administrative Procedure Law art. 69-C

dimensions.conditions: A phone call does not satisfy Article 8’s written-petition condition; particular oral access-to-information requests are separately permitted.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution art. 8; General Transparency Law art. 124

dimensions.conditions: Political petition under Article 8 is reserved to Mexican citizens; nonpolitical access-to-information requests remain available to any person.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts. 8, 33; General Transparency Law art. 124

dimensions.conditions: At the Chamber, register individual lobbyist if lobbying more than once per legislature; accreditation limits, disclosures and no gifts. Senate lobbying activities are reported.
dimensions.legal_basis: Chamber of Deputies Rules arts. 263–267; Senate Rules arts. 298–299

dimensions.conditions: Influencing a legislative decision may be lobbying regardless of medium; apply chamber-specific registration and disclosure rules rather than assume emails exempt.
dimensions.legal_basis: Chamber of Deputies Rules arts. 263–267; Senate Rules arts. 298–299

dimensions.conditions: Chamber rules address individual lobbyists representing private entities, but do not conclusively settle whether a foreign organization’s specific political advocacy is barred as interference; no blanket foreign exemption.
dimensions.legal_basis: Chamber of Deputies Rules arts. 263–264; Constitution art. 33

dimensions.conditions: The cited chamber-specific registration rules do not establish a uniform lobbying regime for every public servant outside the chambers.
dimensions.legal_basis: Chamber of Deputies Rules arts. 263–264; Senate Rules arts. 298–299

dimensions.conditions: Election-day and preceding three days bar dissemination of public electoral campaign propaganda or proselytism; express vote appeals outside campaign stage may be early campaigning.
dimensions.legal_basis: Electoral Procedures Law arts. 3(1)(a), 251(3)–(4)

dimensions.conditions: An ordinary message is not automatically a donation; monetary or in-kind contributions by legal persons to candidates are prohibited, and public electoral propaganda is subject to blackout.
dimensions.legal_basis: Political Parties Law art. 54(1)(f); Electoral Procedures Law art. 251(4)

dimensions.conditions: Foreign persons/legal entities may not contribute money or in kind, directly or indirectly, to candidates or parties; foreign political interference also prohibited. This does not itself ban neutral factual inquiries.
dimensions.legal_basis: Political Parties Law art. 54(1)(d); Constitution art. 33

name: Political contact & verification rules — Mexico
notes: Compliance research summary, not legal advice (14 November 2026). Rows are representative rule combinations, not all 375 purpose/channel/sender/recipient permutations; “any” applies only within the conditions stated. “Fact verification” via transparency law concerns existing documented information, not a duty to confirm or deny new assertions. Article 8 political petitions are reserved to citizens; this does not make every policy email a formal petition. Article 33 is broad but does not precisely classify every foreign organization’s neutral inquiry. For automated and bulk email/phone/social outreach, the [private-sector data law](https://www.diputados.gob.mx/LeyesBiblio/pdf/LFPDPPP.pdf) arts. 5, 9, 15–16, 28–30 remains relevant; publicly listed data need not always require consent (art. 9(II)), but other privacy duties continue. The [consumer law](https://www.diputados.gob.mx/LeyesBiblio/pdf/LFPC.pdf) art. 18 Bis covers consumer advertising opt-outs, not all issue advocacy or a general email-spam prohibition. A direct message is not necessarily public dissemination under the [electoral blackout rule](https://www.diputados.gob.mx/LeyesBiblio/pdf/LGIPE.pdf) art. 251(4); context determines applicability.

dimensions.conditions: No general permission or ban on a foreign organization’s nonpartisan letter was established; check its registration, visa/status and any INGO-specific MoU. Do not infer political campaign permission.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts. 4, 19 (citizen-specific speech); EAD Local NGOs/NPOs Policy 2022 (local NGO scope)

dimensions.conditions: Nonpartisan contact is not itself shown prohibited; foreign nationals do not hold the citizen-specific constitutional speech guarantee. Do not provide prohibited party donations or campaign facilities; comply with electronic-message law.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts. 4, 19; Elections Act 2017 s.204(3); PECA 2016 s.25

dimensions.conditions: An automated call is not a legal person with independent speech rights; human/operator bears responsibility. Telecom anti-spam controls cover calls; avoid unwanted bulk calling.
dimensions.legal_basis: PTA Protection from SPAM, Unsolicited, Fraudulent and Obnoxious Communication Regulations 2009

dimensions.conditions: Ordinary factual inquiry may be made; for an enforceable federal records request, act for/on behalf of an identifiable Pakistani citizen and submit to the designated official, not merely the member.
dimensions.legal_basis: Right of Access to Information Act 2017 ss.2(ii), 3, 9–11

dimensions.conditions: No verified right to compel an elected official to answer a foreign organization’s claim-verification form. Federal RTI applicant must be a Pakistani citizen or someone acting for that citizen.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution art.19A; Right of Access to Information Act 2017 s.2(ii)

dimensions.conditions: For federal records, submit a sufficiently described request to the designated official under the RTI Act; a demand for an official opinion or a confirmation of a claim not in records is not necessarily a records request. Provincial bodies have separate regimes.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution art.19A; Right of Access to Information Act 2017 ss.2, 3, 9–11

dimensions.conditions: Informal asking is not shown banned, but the cited federal statutory access right defines applicant by Pakistani citizenship (or an agent for a Pakistani citizen); no right to compel a spoken answer established.
dimensions.legal_basis: Right of Access to Information Act 2017 ss.2(ii), 3

dimensions.conditions: Peaceful written petition/representation is protected as expression; Pakistan’s Constitution does NOT expressly state a free-standing right to petition an elected official or demand a response.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts.4(2)(b), 19, 19A

dimensions.conditions: A lawful representation may be submitted through an available government form; the cited Constitution does not guarantee a particular form, processing, or response. Formal RTI requests follow separate procedures.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts.4(2)(b), 19A; Right of Access to Information Act 2017 ss.2–3

dimensions.conditions: Nonpartisan advocacy is not shown subject to a general federal lobbyist license; no immunity from other laws, and foreign-funded NGO approved-project/MoU restrictions may apply.
dimensions.legal_basis: Constitution arts.4, 17, 19; EAD Local NGOs/NPOs Policy 2022 paras 6–9, 13

dimensions.conditions: No general federal lobbyist-registration rule or permission for all foreign entities established; organization-specific authorization and anti-corruption constraints require separate review.
dimensions.legal_basis: EAD Local NGOs/NPOs Policy 2022 (scope: local NGOs)

dimensions.conditions: Lawful campaign discussion remains subject to applicable election code, publicity restrictions and PECA; s.182 prohibits public meetings/processions in the specified 48-hour period, not every private online message.
dimensions.legal_basis: Elections Act 2017 ss.180–183; PECA 2016 s.25

dimensions.conditions: Campaign services/facilities may amount to in-kind contributions; observe applicable ECP code and publicity rules. Statutory s.182 meeting/procession blackout is not a blanket ban on private calls.
dimensions.legal_basis: Elections Act 2017 ss.180–183, 204

dimensions.conditions: Contact itself is not categorically barred; foreign-source contributions to a political party (cash or in-kind campaign facilities) are prohibited. Overseas Pakistani NICOP exception applies.
dimensions.legal_basis: Elections Act 2017 s.204(3) and Explanation

dimensions.conditions: Contact itself is not categorically barred; foreign-source contributions to a political party, including paid campaigning or in-kind facilities, are prohibited.
dimensions.legal_basis: Elections Act 2017 s.204(3)–(4)

dimensions.conditions: Responsible operator must avoid misleading/illegal information and commercial marketing contrary to explicit rejection; if a foreign source supplies party campaign facilities, foreign-donation ban may apply. No universal statutory bot ban established.
dimensions.legal_basis: PECA 2016 ss.2(1)(xxxiii), 25; Elections Act 2017 s.204(3)

dimensions.conditions: A system has no separate statutory request right; operator must comply with applicable PECA rules, including prohibitions on harmful/fraudulent/misleading/illegal messaging; no obligation to reply on social media.
dimensions.legal_basis: PECA 2016 s.25

dimensions.conditions: Election campaign publicity is regulated; s.182 bars public meetings/processions during the statutory 48-hour window ending at midnight after the poll. Do not treat this as a blanket ban on every private message or every online post.
dimensions.legal_basis: Elections Act 2017 ss.180, 182–183

name: Political contact & verification rules — Pakistan
notes: Compliance research summary, not legal advice; position as of 2026-11-14. Rows are representative rule-bearing combinations, not the 5×5×5×3 Cartesian product; “any” means the stated rule applies across that axis, not that every possible conduct is permitted. For foreign-source campaign rows, the contribution is prohibited, NOT the bare act of contacting a candidate. Constitution art. 19A and the federal RTI Act establish information-access rights, not a free-standing constitutional right to petition and receive a reply. The 2023 personal-data bill is listed as draft; do not treat its proposed consent provisions as law. Publishing an official work address does not itself establish consent to mass marketing; no general statutory ban on use of all published official contact details was established. No general federal lobbyist-registration statute was verified; parliamentary survey data is internally inconsistent about accredited-lobbyist registers. Foreign NGO project/MoU terms must be checked individually. Election-specific ECP codes and provincial statutes can impose further restrictions.

name: Mexico City — Borough (territorial demarcation)
why_distinct: Mexico City is the national capital and an autonomous federal entity, rather than an ordinary state divided into municipalities. Its 16 territorial demarcations are governed by alcaldías, each consisting of a directly elected mayor and concejo; the mayor runs the local administration, while the concejo oversees government and spending and approves the draft borough budget. Members serve three years, beginning October 1 of the election year.

description: 31 states and Mexico City, together called entidades federativas.
label: GovernmentLevel
name: State / Provincial government

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Aguascalientes
special_status_note: The current governor serves a transitional five-year term (2022–2027) rather than the usual six years, to align election calendars.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Ciudad de México
special_status_note: Federal capital and federal entity, not a state; its executive is the Head of Government and its legislature is the Congress of Mexico City. The 66-member legislature includes one migrant constituency seat.
why_distinct: Mexico City is the national capital and an autonomous federal entity, rather than an ordinary state divided into municipalities. Its 16 territorial demarcations are governed by alcaldías, each consisting of a directly elected mayor and concejo; the mayor runs the local administration, while the concejo oversees government and spending and approves the draft borough budget. Members serve three years, beginning October 1 of the election year.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Quintana Roo
special_status_note: The current governor serves a transitional five-year term (2022–2027) rather than the usual six years, to align election calendars.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Sinaloa
special_status_note: Graciela Domínguez Nava was appointed interim governor by the state congress on 2026-08-25 following Rubén Rocha Moya’s indefinite leave; she is expected to complete the term ending 2027-10-31.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave
researched_name: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave

council_name: Local council (municipal or metropolitan corporation council; tehsil, town or union council according to locality)
description: Province-specific elected local-government structures include metropolitan or municipal corporations, municipal and town committees, and union, village or neighbourhood councils; no verified, consistent nationwide 2026 count of governing bodies. The 2023 census lists 650 urban areas, which must not be equated with 650 municipal governments.
label: GovernmentLevel
name: Municipal / Local government
unit_name: Local government (municipal corporation, town corporation, municipal committee, tehsil council or union council, depending on province)

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Islamabad Capital Territory — Town corporation (2026 delimitation, contested)
why_distinct: Federally administered capital, not a provincial municipality. The 2026 ordinance proposed three town corporations with union councils and indirectly chosen mayors, and 130 union councils were delimited. By 14 November 2026 the ordinance had lapsed; the 2015 one-metropolitan-corporation/125-union-council framework had revived and the High Court suspended the election schedule. The three listed towns are the published 2026 delimitations, NOT confirmed functioning elected councils; none has a confirmed incumbent mayor. The operative boundaries remain before the court.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Karachi Division — Town municipal corporation (town)
why_distinct: Three-tier urban local government: Karachi Metropolitan Corporation/City Council, 25 town municipal corporations and their town councils, and union committees. Unlike an ordinary standalone municipality, the metropolitan body overlays town-level councils; town chairmen are selected by the town councils rather than directly by residents. The names below are the 2023 returned town heads; a town-by-town 2026 incumbency confirmation is unavailable for some, so later replacements cannot be ruled out. Four-year terms run from oath, but an exact end date is not confirmed for each head.

description: Intermediate administrative units, not first-level federating units. Last nationwide official count verified is dated 1 March 2023; the 2026 total may differ.
label: GovernmentLevel
name: State / Provincial government

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Gilgit-Baltistan
special_status_note: Federally administered, self-governing territory under the Gilgit-Baltistan Order 2018, not a constitutionally established Pakistani province. Its assembly has 24 directly elected and nine indirectly elected reserved seats.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Islamabad
special_status_note: Federally administered capital territory, not a province: the federally appointed Chief Commissioner administers it under the Interior Division. It has no territorial legislature or chief minister; Pakistan’s Parliament legislates for the territory.
why_distinct: Federally administered capital, not a provincial municipality. The 2026 ordinance proposed three town corporations with union councils and indirectly chosen mayors, and 130 union councils were delimited. By 14 November 2026 the ordinance had lapsed; the 2015 one-metropolitan-corporation/125-union-council framework had revived and the High Court suspended the election schedule. The three listed towns are the published 2026 delimitations, NOT confirmed functioning elected councils; none has a confirmed incumbent mayor. The operative boundaries remain before the court.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Azad Jammu and Kashmir
special_status_note: Self-governing territory under its 1974 Interim Constitution, not a Pakistani province. Its executive is called Prime Minister; 12 of the 45 general assembly seats represent refugees resident in Pakistan. Seven constituency elections had been postponed at the August 2026 prime-ministerial vote.

label: GovernmentLevel
name: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
special_status_note: Governor’s rule and emergency imposed on 2026-10-11: Sohail Afridi remains the listed but non-functional Chief Minister, reportedly in preventive custody, while Governor Faisal Karim Kundi exercises provincial executive powers. This is not an acting-chief-minister appointment.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Municipal councillor
selection_details: Seats filled by election on winning slates and proportional representation under state rules, or by indigenous community electoral procedures. Usually three years, but some states have four-year councils and indigenous customary systems may prescribe one, one-and-a-half, two or three years.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Municipal President
selection_details: Elected with the municipal slate by popular vote; indigenous customary-system municipalities choose authorities under their own community rules. A substitute can assume office on leave of the elected president. Usually three years, but some states have four-year councils and indigenous customary systems may prescribe one, one-and-a-half, two or three years.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Municipal trustee
selection_details: Elected on municipal slates, with some states providing a proportional-representation trustee; indigenous customary-system selection also exists. Usually three years, but some states have four-year councils and indigenous customary systems may prescribe one, one-and-a-half, two or three years.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Federal Deputy (single-member district)
selection_details: Plurality vote in one of 300 federal districts

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Federal Deputy (proportional representation list)
selection_details: Elected by popular vote for party lists in 5 multi-state circumscriptions

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of the Chamber of Deputies
selection_details: Elected by deputies to preside over the chamber for a legislative year.
title_local: Presidenta o Presidente de la Mesa Directiva de la Cámara de Diputados

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Circuit magistrate
selection_details: Direct popular election within judicial circuits; renewable for consecutive nine-year terms. 464 posts were contested in 2025, not the systemwide total.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: District judge
selection_details: Direct popular election within judicial circuits; renewable for consecutive nine-year terms. 386 posts were contested in 2025, not the systemwide total.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Electoral magistrate, regional chambers
selection_details: Five regional chambers of three; direct popular election by electoral constituency. The 2025 elected cohort is reported by the tribunal for 2025–2033 under transitional provisions.
title_local: Magistrada o Magistrado Electoral de las Salas Regionales

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Electoral magistrate, Superior Chamber
selection_details: Nationwide direct popular vote; ordinary six-year nonrenewable term, subject to transitional rules for sitting and newly elected magistrates.
title_local: Magistrada o Magistrado Electoral de la Sala Superior

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of the Electoral Tribunal
selection_details: Presidency rotates according to popular vote ranking under reformed Constitution Article 99; not the president of the Supreme Court.
title_local: Presidenta o Presidente del Tribunal Electoral

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Member of the Judicial Administration Body
selection_details: One designated by the President, one by a two-thirds vote of senators present, and three by six Supreme Court votes.
title_local: Integrante del Pleno del Órgano de Administración Judicial

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of the Judicial Administration Body
selection_details: Rotating two-year leadership from among its five appointed members, under applicable law.
title_local: Presidenta o Presidente del Órgano de Administración Judicial

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Judicial discipline magistrate
selection_details: Direct nationwide popular vote; staggered, nonrenewable six-year terms.
title_local: Magistrada o Magistrado del Tribunal de Disciplina Judicial

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of the Judicial Discipline Tribunal
selection_details: Two-year rotation according to votes won in the popular judicial election.
title_local: Presidenta o Presidente del Tribunal de Disciplina Judicial

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Electoral councillor
selection_details: Chosen by two-thirds of deputies present via constitutionally specified selection procedure; staggered nine-year nonrenewable terms.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of the General Council
selection_details: Ordinarily chosen by two-thirds of deputies present for a nonrenewable nine-year term; on a definitive vacancy, councillors internally elect a provisional president until the Chamber selects a replacement.
title_local: Consejera Presidenta o Consejero Presidente del Consejo General

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Head of the Agency for Digital Transformation and Telecommunications
selection_details: Executive agency listed separately from the 21 secretariats in Article 26; presidential appointment.
title_local: Titular de la Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of Mexico
selection_details: Direct nationwide popular election, single six-year term, no reelection.
title_local: Presidenta o Presidente de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Secretary of State
selection_details: Heads of the 21 secretariats listed in Article 26 of the Organic Law; appointed/removed by the President, with constitutional exceptions to confirmation.

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of the Senate
selection_details: Elected from among senators by absolute majority of members present, by ballot; serves one legislative year.
title_local: Presidenta o Presidente de la Mesa Directiva del Senado de la República

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Senator (relative majority)
selection_details: Two seats per state for the most-voted formula

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Senator (first minority)
selection_details: One seat per state for the runner-up party's formula

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Senator (proportional representation list)
selection_details: Elected by popular vote for national party lists

label: PoliticalOffice
name: Justice of the Supreme Court
selection_details: Nationwide direct, secret popular vote; ordinary twelve-year nonrenewable term. The first elected cohort beginning 2025 has transitional eight- and eleven-year terms.
title_local: Ministra o Ministro de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación

label: PoliticalOffice
name: President of the Supreme Court
selection_details: Rotates every two years among elected justices by number of popular votes received.
title_local: Presidenta o Presidente de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación
